gaps.sentence: It was ___ dull a lecture that people walked out.
gaps.explanation: so + adjective (+a + noun) + that… — the alternative emphatic pattern.

gaps.sentence: We had the walls ___ last month.
gaps.explanation: 'have something done' = arrange for it to be done: had the walls painted.

gaps.sentence: Her success was largely ___ to her coach.
gaps.explanation: 'be down to somebody/something' = be caused by.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ many customers for the staff to serve properly.
gaps.explanation: 'Too many … to …' — excess preventing an outcome.

gaps.sentence: The museum charges for entry; ___, under-twenties visit free.
gaps.explanation: 'However' marks the contrast between paying and free.

gaps.sentence: The first edition of the book ___ out in 1998.
The meeting has been ___ forward to Monday.
gaps.explanation: 'bring forward' = move to an earlier time (opposite of put off).

gaps.sentence: No sooner had he arrived ___ it started to rain.
